# Assignments {.unnumbered}

All graded work for the course is listed here. Dates and details will be posted as each item is released. The weights below follow the (tentative) [assessment scheme](./course.qmd#assessment).

## Homeworks

Five homeworks, together worth **20%**. Each carries 50 points, in five problems.
Problem sets are distributed as PDF; solution sets are posted after the
submission deadline. HW 1 is **graded for completion** — credit is for a genuine
attempt at every part rather than for correct answers. HW 2 onwards are **graded
on correctness**, with marks carried by the reasoning as much as the answer.

| # | Topic | Released | Due | Problems | Solutions |
|:---:|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|
| HW 1 | Random variables, joints, conditionals, Bayes | Mon 10 Aug 2026 | Tue 18 Aug 2026, in class | [PDF](./homeworks/hw1.pdf) | [PDF](./homeworks/hw1-solutions.pdf) |
| HW 2 | Distributions and maximum likelihood | Mon 10 Aug 2026 | Tue 25 Aug 2026, in class | [PDF](./homeworks/hw2.pdf) | after deadline |
| HW 3 | — | TBA | TBA | — | — |
| HW 4 | — | TBA | TBA | — | — |
| HW 5 | — | TBA | TBA | — | — |

: {tbl-colwidths="[8,34,14,14,15,15]"}

Solution sets are worked derivations rather than answer keys: each problem states
the concept it is testing and derives the answer in full.

## Practice sheets

Not graded, and not submitted. Each sheet derives a small set of results in full and
ends with exercises — read it with a pen and redo the derivations yourself. These
are the computations the lectures assume you can do, so they are worth the time even
though no marks depend on them.

Practice 2 has a companion you can play with: **[The Walk Lab](./materials/walk-lab.html)**,
also embedded in the tutorial [The Random Walk](./tutorials/20-random-walk.qmd).

| # | Topic | Posted | Sheet |
|:---:|---|---|:---:|
| Practice 1 | Gaussian algebra and $q(x_t \mid x_0)$; conditional expectation as the squared-error minimiser; KL between Gaussians | Tue 18 Aug 2026 | [PDF](./homeworks/practice_01.pdf) |
| Practice 2 | The random walk: its exact law by counting, the heat equation, and a reverse step you can solve in closed form | Fri 21 Aug 2026 | [PDF](./homeworks/practice_02.pdf) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,52,18,18]"}
